source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether the incident ray, normal, and reflected ray must lie in the same plane.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: incident ray is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: When the sheet is flat, the incident and reflected beams can lie on the same plane.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when When the sheet is flat, the incident and reflected beams can lie on the same plane is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane. same-plane alignment allows the reflected beam to be seen on the flat sheet The learner explains that the incident ray, normal, and reflected ray lie in the same plane and uses the bent-sheet observation as evidence. The reflected beam should stay visible anywhere on the same sheet because bending the sheet does not matter.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Light: mirrors and lenses. The student must decide: Decide whether the incident ray, normal, and reflected ray must lie in the same plane. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
